recap_lines: Responsibility for an AI failure is a distribution, not a suspect list.
A sign-off has substance only when a person with stakes answers for it.
A check counts only when it comes from outside the system checked.
Kantian weighs capacity times duty, utilitarian weighs leverage on outcomes.
An attestation states what was NOT tested, and the signer can withhold.
Regime failures come from the rules, not the algorithm, and a regime can be changed.
bookends.segment: Name The Term, Rule Out The Look-Alike
bookends.command: Quiz me on accountability terms for AI systems. Give me one short case at a time. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Draw on responsibility gap, shape versus substance, answerability, common cause failure, validator independence, audit trail, attestation, authority to withhold and regime failure. Hold back the answer until I reply, then correct me.
checks: Check: each case fits one term and names the look-alike it rules out.
Check: no answer appears before you have given your own.

beats.act: Why a human, not more AI
beats.narration_text: Two timelines. The person's line runs unbroken through two decisions to the question, why did you decide that. The model's line is three separate sessions. Episodic memory is recall of your own past in context. Semantic memory is recall of facts, where AI is superhuman. For example, ask a job seeker why she turned down an offer last spring, and she recalls the interview and the salary talk. An AI assistant can recite facts about that company, but a fresh session holds no memory of advising her.
